starting_points: Start with Auto Gain off, a moderate ratio, and threshold set so only the intended events move the gain-reduction meter.
Treat attack and release as envelope-shaping controls; exaggerate briefly to learn, then back off and level-match.
Use the minimum gain reduction or range that solves the named problem across representative sections.
stop_rule: Stop or back off as soon as the named envelope/level problem improves but attacks, expression, groove, tone, noise, or depth become worse.
teaching_principle: Bus and multiband compression trade global movement and density against transient integrity, depth, phase, and section contrast.
title: When should I trust Auto Release
tradeoffs_and_risks: More control can reduce transient impact, expression, depth, or groove.
Makeup gain and saturation can bias the A/B and reduce headroom.
Fast or deep action can expose noise, sibilance, bleed, pumping, or distortion.
undo_or_reset: Restore the saved compressor state, bypass/remove the temporary instance, and match output to the original.
user_language_aliases: program-dependent recovery can help but may not follow the desired groove
what_to_listen_for: The intended envelope or level problem should improve without flattening expression, dulling attacks, exaggerating noise, or changing groove unintentionally.
The active version should remain preferable after manual output matching and in the full arrangement.
Gain reduction should recover in a way that supports the phrase or pulse rather than following a memorized number.
